brief.lead: Learn how Terasweep reuses model fits and scores. Follow the original Ridge investigation from its reference to a billion-trial experiment, then see the shared sweep applied to four models.

Start with the two studies.

The original Ridge investigation measures the effect of each optimization, including AVX-512. The later matched sweep benchmarks use the same scalar scorer for each model and its reference. Ridge, DLinear, LightGBM, and TiDE each ran one billion sampled trials on an M1 Max.

reference.lead: Match the model, inputs, and metric contract before interpreting a speed ratio. This chapter starts with the original Ridge reference.

Matched references for the four-model runner

Use the model cards to see how predictions are checked against Limen Ridge, Limen DLinear, official LightGBM, and Google Research TiDE. The later matched sweep calibration refits the reference model on every trial and uses Terasweep's scalar scorer on both paths. scale.lead: See where the time goes as each study scales from thousands to a billion sampled trials.
scale.prepend:
Four matched sweeps on Apple M1 Max

Each model used 256 training and 128 test rows from its retained market-data fixture. All nine Terasweep sweep sizes from 10 through one billion were measured with compact scalar scoring. All billion-trial runs completed with zero failed rows. Each draw reused an existing fit when its training settings matched.

The uncached reference fits afresh for every trial. Both paths use the same input, trial order, and scalar scoring contract. The measured reference prefixes agree on predictions within the stated tolerances and agree exactly on signals and the reported winners. LightGBM and TiDE predictions are bit-identical in these checks.

Beyond the largest measured reference, each card projects the reference time from the observed per-trial cost plus one backend setup. The Terasweep column measures work after input loading, including backend setup and winner details. The historical explorer below uses whole-process timings on a different Ridge workload and host.
